uncertainties: The admonishing voice continues through verse 29, but the speaker's exact identity should not be inferred solely from the gray color.
The wife's confession in verse 51 is explicitly marked. The attribution of verses 52-53 remains unassigned; do not extend her quotation into them by default.
Joseph's response is described as concealed; underlined quotation signs distinguish the inner response from an audible dialogue turn.
The speaker of وأوتينا العلم من قبلها وكنا مسلمين is not fixed by the queen's preceding answer. The added quotation ends before this clause.
The argument interleaves opponent claims and two قل responses. The beta marks the two explicit responses but does not assign the intervening أن يؤتى clause to a speaker by punctuation alone.
The purpose clause وليبتلي الله after the last قل response is left outside its narrow scope; whether the explanation remains part of that response requires discourse review.
The scope of قل relative to the description of earlier recipients and their praise is not fixed by a verse boundary. The first command is marked; the following narrated description remains separate.
ربهم أعلم بهم may be the first group's statement or narratorial comment. The current proposal ends before it; a different reading would extend that quotation.
The messenger's reply contains the reported divine first-person words through ورحمة منا. The final وكان أمرا مقضيا is left outside both quotations pending a narration/continuation decision.
The inmates' بلى is marked as a brief reply. Whether ولكن حقت كلمة العذاب continues their answer or is commentary remains open.
The angels' assurance is quoted through the welcome in verse 32. The attribution of the final نزلا من غفور رحيم formula can be reviewed separately without changing the preceding clear angelic speech.
